functions.name: addManifest
functions.description: Adds a Kubernetes manifest to be applied to the Kind cluster via `kubectl apply`.
functions.remarks:
The manifest is applied after the parent Kind cluster reaches the
`Running` state. Downstream resources that call
`WaitFor` on the manifest resource only start once `kubectl apply` succeeds.
Requires `kubectl` on `PATH`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the manifest resource.

parameters.name: manifestPath
parameters.description: Absolute path to a Kubernetes manifest file, a directory of manifest files, or a Kustomize overlay directory. Relative paths are not supported. URL fetch is not supported; reference a local file or directory.

functions.remarks:
Use this when the cluster control plane can take longer than the default 60 seconds
to begin serving the Kubernetes API, such as on slower developer machines or busy CI hosts.

functions.name: withCrdWaitRetry
functions.description: Retries Helm installs that race newly-created CRDs which have not reached the `Established` condition yet.
functions.remarks:
This is useful for charts that create CRDs and immediately render custom resources
that depend on those CRDs. Between attempts, Kind waits for newly observed CRDs
to report `Established`.
functions.signature: withCrdWaitRetry(maxAttempts?: number, backoff?: timespan, crdWaitTimeout?: timespan): KindHelmChartResource

parameters.name: maxAttempts
parameters.description: The total number of install attempts. Must be 2 or greater.

parameters.name: backoff
parameters.description: The initial delay before retrying. Later retries back off exponentially. When `null`, Kind uses a 5 second initial backoff.

parameters.name: crdWaitTimeout
parameters.description: The timeout used while waiting for newly discovered CRDs to become `Established` between retry attempts. When `null`, Kind uses a 5 minute timeout.

functions.name: withKind
functions.description: Configures the Kubernetes environment to create and deploy to a local Kind cluster. Enables `aspire deploy` to provision the cluster, load container images, and install the generated Helm chart.
functions.returns: A reference to the `IResourceBuilder`1` for further Kind-specific configuration.

functions.name: withKindClusterReference
functions.description: Configures a non-container resource to reference the Kind cluster by injecting kubeconfig environment variables.
functions.remarks:
This overload sets `KUBECONFIG` to the host kubeconfig path, which is appropriate for
resources that execute on the host (e.g., executables, projects).
For container resources, use the `WithReference`
overload instead, which handles container-specific requirements like bind-mounting and network connectivity.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The Kind cluster resource builder.

functions.name: withKindContainerReference
functions.description: Configures a container resource to reference the Kind cluster by bind-mounting the container-compatible kubeconfig, injecting environment variables, and connecting to the Kind container network.
functions.remarks:
This overload is the primary integration path for containers. It:
-
-
-
-
The container-compatible kubeconfig uses the Kind control-plane container name
(`{clusterName}-control-plane`) instead of `127.0.0.1`, enabling container-to-container
communication over the Kind container network.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The Kind cluster resource builder.

functions.name: withKindNetwork
functions.description: Connects a container resource to the Kind container network, enabling it to communicate with the Kind cluster's API server and nodes.
functions.remarks:
Use this method when a container needs direct network connectivity to the Kind control plane.
Kind creates a separate container network ("kind") for its nodes. Aspire manages
its own container network for containers it creates. Containers on different
networks cannot communicate by default.
Aspire does not provide a built-in way to add containers to additional container networks,
and `WithContainerRuntimeArgs("--network", "kind")` is overridden internally.
See for the upstream feature request.
This method works around the limitation by subscribing to the container's stopped event.
When the container stops (typically because it can't reach the Kind cluster), the hook
connects the container to the "kind" network via the configured container runtime and
restarts it.
If the container does not already have an explicit name (via `WithContainerName`),
this method assigns one using the pattern `{resource.Name}-{random}` to ensure
the container can be identified by the handler.

functions.name: withKubernetesVersion
functions.description: Sets the Kubernetes version for the Kind cluster.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The Kubernetes version (e.g., "v1.32.2").

functions.name: withNamespace
functions.description: Sets the Kubernetes namespace for the deployment.
functions.remarks:
Helm chart resources pass `--create-namespace`. Manifest resources only pass
`--namespace` to `kubectl apply`; they do not create the namespace.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: The Kubernetes namespace.

functions.name: withNodeImage
functions.description: Sets the Kind node image for every node in the cluster.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: The fully qualified Kind node image, such as `kindest/node:v1.33.1`. This overrides the image that would otherwise be derived from `WithKubernetesVersion``1`.

functions.name: withNodeMount
functions.description: Adds an extra host mount to every Kind node container.
functions.remarks:
This configures Kind node-container mounts, which are useful for surfacing host-side assets
such as local manifest directories, certificates, or other development-time inputs to workloads
that later mount paths from the node filesystem.
functions.signature: withNodeMount(hostPath: string, containerPath: string, readOnly?: boolean): IKindResource

parameters.name: hostPath
parameters.description: The path on the host. Relative paths are resolved against the AppHost directory before being written to the Kind config.

parameters.name: containerPath
parameters.description: The absolute path inside the Kind node container.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description: `true` to mount the path read-only.

functions.name: withServerSideApply
functions.description: Applies the manifest server-side (maps to `kubectl apply --server-side`). Required for large CRDs that exceed the client-side annotation size limit.

parameters.name: forceConflicts
parameters.description: When `true`, also passes `--force-conflicts` to override field ownership held by another field manager (e.g., a controller). Defaults to `false`.

functions.name: withWorkerNodes
functions.description: Sets the number of worker nodes for the Kind cluster.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of worker nodes. Must be zero or greater.
